messages:
Maya: heads up — ran into a weird one during localtest with dockerized sample app, seems like redwoodctl tokens are getting stomped across profiles when mounting ~/.redwood into the container

Jamal: ugh, that sounds bad. repro steps?

Maya: steps: 1) have two local profiles (default + sandbox) 2) run app container that mounts my host ~/.redwood 3) app inside container runs redwoodctl localserve login --profile sandbox 4) host default profile token now points at the sandbox token, causing host CLI to fail login

Maya: minimal command i used:
```bash
docker run --rm -it -v $HOME/.redwood:/root/.redwood -v $(pwd):/app my-sample-app /bin/bash
# inside container
redwoodctl login --profile sandbox --headless
```

Jamal: ok that explains it — the mounted dir is literally shared. redwoodctl stores tokens by profile name in the same path so two separate runtimes writing the same files will collide

Sara: is this a redwoodctl bug or just expected docker hygiene? either way we should avoid leaking host token stores into ephemeral containers by default in our samples

Maya: agreed. the surprising part is our localtest/quickstart docs recommend mounting ~/.redwood for convenience, which is what i followed. that makes the default sample apps unsafe for users with multiple profiles

Jamal: short-term workaround: set REDWOOD_HOME to an app-local path inside container and mount a dedicated dir, e.g. `-e REDWOOD_HOME=/tmp/redwood && -v $(pwd)/ci/redwood:/tmp/redwood`

Sara: long-term fix ideas:
- update quickstart to not suggest mounting host token dir; use example with REDWOOD_HOME or explicit --profile and ephemeral token dir
- make redwoodctl write token files with a process-unique suffix when running in headless/CI mode (eg `/root/.redwood/tokens-sandbox.<pid>`), and keep an explicit symlink mapping file so non-colliding runs are default
- add detection: if REDWOOD_HOME is mounted from outside, warn when login would overwrite other profile tokens

Maya: here's a tiny patch i tested locally that warns when $REDWOOD_HOME contains more than one active token file and login would overwrite: (pseudo)
```go
if countTokens(REDWOOD_HOME) > 1 && !forceOverwrite {
  fmt.Println("warning: this REDWOOD_HOME appears shared; consider using --profile or REDWOOD_HOME per-run")
}
```

devex-bot: created issue #3421: "redwoodctl: avoid token collisions when REDWOOD_HOME is shared by containers" and assigned to @jamal for triage :spiral_note_pad:

Jamal: i'll pick this up. plan: update quickstart docs + add runtime warning + RFC for token namespacing. will write unit test for migration behavior so existing installs keep working

ci-bot: scheduled CI job `devex/redwoodctl-token-isolation` to run on jamal/new-token-namespacing branch

Maya: thanks — can you also add a short blurb to onboarding checklist? new hires following sample apps tripped over this

Sara: added to onboarding checklist PR draft. thanks for reporting @Maya :thumbsup:
